newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cyprus talks invitations to be sent in next few days.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus talks invitations to be sent in next few days.

text.p: Invitations to the leaders of the two Cypriot communities to attend talks under U.N. auspices will go out within the "next day or two," Secretary-General Kofi Annan said Tuesday.
"We are going to do it in the next day or two. It should be in the next few days," he said.
Answering reporters' questions after briefing the Security Council on a number of mostly African issues, he added: "We would expect to have the meeting in early July."

The talks are to involve Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides, as head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash. This will be their first known encounter for nearly three years.
A U.N. spokesman said recently the talks would begin July 9, but this has yet to be confirmed.

Asked about the venue of the Clerides-Denktash meeting, which the United Nations is anxious to keep secluded, the secretary-general said jokingly: "Let's say it will be on this side of the Atlantic, and it will be outside New York City."
Asked how far outside the city, he replied: "It will be two hours outside New York." He did not say in which direction.
Annan declined to comment on the forthcoming negotiations, aimed at reuniting the divided island as a bi-communal, bi-communal federation.
